This study reports empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM analyses comparing individuals with cocaine-use disorder (a stimulant class) to healthy controls. It uses whole-brain, voxelwise modulated GMV analyses (FSL-VBM, randomise) and reports significant between-group clusters (tables/figures/supplement) differentiating CUD from HC, satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain contrast. The paper provides grey-matter volume measures (modulated GMV), details of MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant demographics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not an atlas/parcellation-only analysis, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/supplement referenced). Thus the study qualifies for inclusion as a stimulant (cocaine) substance-use structural MRI comparison with controls.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis users and non-users and reports gray-matter measures (cortical thickness, gray matter density, regional volumes) (meets I4, I5). However, the paper’s analyses derive regional/parcel-based results using an atlas-based multi-atlas parcellation (Neuromorphometrics) and report per-region averages rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with peak coordinates. No whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts yielding surviving significant clusters with reported (x,y,z) coordinates are provided (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (atlas/parcellation-based results only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 flexible factorial and planned whole-brain t-tests) that yielded significant clusters with reported coordinates (see Table 2 and figures) showing GMV differences (left IFG and bilateral vmPFC). Methods (4T scanner, SPM8, VBM8 preprocessing) and participant demographics are reported. Therefore it satisfies whole-brain voxelwise reporting with significant peak coordinates and provides the required GM measures for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent (AD) patients and healthy controls, reporting voxelwise analyses and a between-group whole-brain contrast (voxel-wise two-sample t-test within a right-hemispheric mask) with significant clusters and peak coordinates (x=7.5, y=-51, z=1.5; cluster size reported) after cluster-level FWE correction. Grey-matter measures are modulated VBM (volume/density), MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistics (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported, and participant demographics and substance-use measures are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing heavy cannabis users to controls and reporting voxelwise grey-matter results. It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., medial temporal lobe/hippocampus-amygdala at x=-27,y=-10,z=-20 and superior temporal gyrus at x=-52,y=11,z=-15; pFWE<.05), satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain contrast with coordinates. Grey-matter measurements (GM volume/density) were used and preprocessing/MRI details (3T scanner, VBM8/SPM, DARTEL) and participant characteristics are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine users and controls that reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses and voxel-wise DTI results. Cortical thickness is an accepted grey-matter measure per I5. The paper describes vertex-wise and voxel-wise whole-brain contrasts and refers to significant clusters presented in Supplementary Figures/Tables (Supplementary Table 2, Supplementary Figure 2, Supplementary Figure 3, Supplementary Table 3, Supplementary Table 4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain statistical maps and significant foci (I6–I8). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/statistical details are reported (I9). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4–I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or atlas-parcellation-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary tables are referenced for coordinates.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between heavy adolescent alcohol users and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports voxelwise analyses (VBM) and significant between-group clusters (ROI-restricted voxelwise analyses with small-volume correction) in ACC, orbitofrontal/frontopolar cortex, superior temporal gyrus and insula; results are presented in figures and a table with MNI coordinates. It therefore meets whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements (I6) as the meta-analysis allows sub-volume voxelwise maps with reported coordinates. The study also meets I4 (empirical MRI), I5 (GM volume measure), I7 (significant foci with reported peaks), I8 (results reported in tables/figures), and I9 (participant demographics and MRI parameters reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) and I6 (must report a whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrast). The study does satisfy I5 (GM volume measured via VBM), I7 (reports significant voxelwise clusters with peak coordinates), I8 (results available in tables/figures), and I9 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

The manuscript is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing amphetamine-type stimulant users and controls and reports vertexwise whole-brain analyses of cortical thickness and cortical volume. Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM study), I5 (GM measures including cortical thickness/volume), and I6 (whole-brain vertexwise statistical maps via Freesurfer QDEC). However, criterion I7 requires that at least one whole-brain contrast yields a significant cluster with reported peak coordinates (x,y,z). Although the text states significant clusters survived multiple-comparison correction, the provided full text does not include the peak coordinate tables/figures or explicit coordinate values (results are referenced as being in figures/tables/supplementary materials but these are not present). Because I7 cannot be verified from the supplied content and the coordinate information appears omitted, I cannot confirm the primary requirement for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore I exclude this record due to incomplete reporting of required coordinate data in the supplied full text (fulltext_incomplete=true).

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI study (surface-based FreeSurfer analyses) comparing substance users (ALC, ALC+CU) to controls and reports a vertex-wise whole-hemisphere analysis with a significant cluster in right medial orbitofrontal cortex (p<.001). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study), I5 (grey-matter surface-based measure — surface area), I6 (whole-brain vertex-wise analysis was performed), and I8 (voxel/vertex-wise results are reported in the manuscript text). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the paper, as provided, does not report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach x,y,z) for the significant whole-brain/vertex-wise cluster(s). The meta-analysis requires reported peak coordinates for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it is an empirical MRI paper that performed VBM processing (so a gray-matter measure was computed) and reports participant demographics and MRI details, it does NOT report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts of gray-matter differences with significant peak coordinates. Specifically, it lacks (a) a reported whole-brain GM volume/density between-group result (I4 not met), (b) a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with reported coordinates (I6 not met), and (c) any significant GM foci/peak coordinates from such contrasts (I7 not met). In addition, the substance studied (betel quid/areca) is outside the five target pharmacological classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants) addressed by the meta-analysis, so the study does not address the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study computed gray-matter measures via VBM) and I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: none of E5–E7. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study performed whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (methods describe whole-brain spatial normalization and SPM99 t tests) and reports significant clusters (corrected p<0.01, t and extent thresholds) in prefrontal, insular, and temporal regions, with results referenced in Table 2 and figures (meets I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, non-empirical, or multivariate-classifier-only study). Therefore the study should be included.

The analysis used FIRST segmentation to extract regional (per-structure) volumes and performed region-wise/statistical tests (MANCOVA, post-hoc tests) rather than whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts. Therefore it fails the key whole-brain/coordinate-based inclusion criteria (I6 and I7) and must be excluded under exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI/region-based results) and E6 (per-region/parcellation analysis rather than voxelwise).

It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI study comparing groups), I5 (reports cortical thickness/volume/surface-based GM measures), I6 (performed vertexwise whole-brain contrasts), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and processing pipeline). However, the full text provided does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the significant whole-brain clusters; I7 (reporting of at least one significant focus with peak coordinates) is not satisfied. Because I7 is required, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered by the article. Full text appears complete.

No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Because failure to meet I7 is sufficient for exclusion from the coordinate-based meta-analysis, the study must be excluded based on the information provided.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls (SPM5/VBM5; 1.5T). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests (FDR-corrected) showing widespread significant GM reductions in alcoholics versus controls, and exploratory voxelwise regressions linking IGT performance to regional GM (with peaks plotted in MNI space and anatomical localization described). Although specific coordinate tables/figures are referenced rather than embedded in the provided text, the manuscript explicitly states peak coordinates were plotted and results are available in figures/tables, which satisfies the allowance for coordinates in tables/figures (I8). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical structural MRI study comparing cocaine users and controls and uses cortical thickness measures (inclusion met: I4, I5). It reports MRI field strength and preprocessing software (I9). However, the imaging analysis is surface-based ROI/parcellation using the Desikan–Killiany atlas (mean thickness per region) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map, and no voxel/vertex coordinates or peak foci are reported. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates (inclusion I6 and I7 not met). This violates exclusion criteria E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation) and E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded.

The study uses a cortical grey-matter measure (cortical thickness), performs a vertexwise whole-brain analysis (with multiple-comparison correction), and indicates detailed cluster information (reported in tables/figures/supplement), which satisfies the requirement for significant whole-brain foci (reported peak information acceptable if in tables/supplement). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, field strength, and processing software are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, atlas-only parcellation results only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

It reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software, and substance-use measures (pack-years). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas/parcellation-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Therefore it does NOT meet I7 (no significant whole-brain foci reported) and must be excluded per E5 (only ROI-significant results / no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (between-group results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than from significant voxelwise/vertexwise clusters). This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing substance-using (Antisocial Substance Dependence) male adolescents to matched controls. It reports gray-matter volume (modulated GM images) and performed whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster-level correction, yielding significant clusters. The paper provides peak coordinates for several analyses (e.g., within-patient SUMDEP negative association in left DLPFC: MNI X = -45, Y = 16, Z = 33; patient impulsivity: X = 45, Y = -34, Z = 33) and describes between-group significant clusters (left DLPFC, cerebellum, precuneus) consistent with voxelwise results likely tabulated in the manuscript. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5) are reported. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Thus it satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing MDMA (a stimulant) users to controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and figures, the provided full text does not report numeric peak coordinates (x,y,z) for significant clusters. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study), I5 (gray-matter measure: gray matter concentration), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis performed), I8 (results indicated in figures/SPMs), I9 (participant age/sex and methods reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (the paper, as provided, does not report peak coordinates for significant clusters). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Because I7 is required, the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis unless peak coordinates can be obtained from the full text, tables, figures, or by contacting authors.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between substance-dependent individuals (SDI) and controls (I4, I5). The study performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with cluster-level FWE correction and reports significant between-group clusters with peak coordinates in MNI space (e.g., −5, 53, −3) (I6, I7, I8). Participant demographics, substance use characteristics (including cocaine and amphetamine—stimulants—and alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (I9). The paper is a full-text empirical article (not ROI-only; whole-brain results are primary), so no exclusion criteria apply (E5–E7 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion requirements for contribution of voxelwise coordinates to the meta-analysis of structural GM differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing individuals with prenatal alcohol exposure (FASD) to matched controls using surface-based cortical thickness measures. The study performed vertexwise whole-brain analyses (CIVET pipeline) and reports significant between-group cortical thickness reductions in multiple regions, with cluster information and peak vertex MNI coordinates listed. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), acquisition and preprocessing (CIVET, smoothing, SurfStat) and statistical methods are described. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I5 (GM measure: cortical thickness), I6 (whole-brain vertexwise contrast), I7 (significant clusters with reported peak coordinates), I8 (results available in text/tables/supplement), and I9 (reporting of age/sex and MRI/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-only parcellation as sole whole-brain map, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM2 VBM), provides multiple significant clusters with peak coordinates in MNI space, and quantifies GM volume reductions. Participant demographics, substance-use history, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it satisfies whole-brain voxelwise reporting with significant foci and adequate methodological detail relevant for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM alterations in substance users.

This study reports empirical English-language MRI comparisons of grey matter between substance-dependent and control subjects (I4 met), uses acceptable grey-matter measures including cortical thickness (I5 met), and reports participant and methods details (I9 met). However, all structural analyses are ROI-based using FreeSurfer parcellation (mean regional volumes and cortical thickness per Desikan-Killiany-style labels), and results are reported as region-level differences rather than voxelwise/vertexwise statistical maps with peak coordinates. The paper does not provide whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with reported MNI/Talairach coordinates (I6 not met; I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical MRI study reporting manual ROI-based cingulate grey matter volumes in cannabis-using vs non-using ARMS/FEP patients. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study comparing substance users vs controls) and I5 (grey-matter volume measure); I9 (study reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength and statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps or peak coordinates; results derive from manual region-of-interest analyses (cingulum subdivisions) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from this voxelwise coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Exclusion E5 and E6: the study reports only ROI/parcellation-based results using the FreeSurfer Desikan–Killiany atlas (per-region average cortical area/volume/thickness) rather than a voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain statistical map with peak coordinates. Inclusion met: I4 (empirical English structural MRI study of substance users vs controls) and I5 (grey-matter measures include cortical thickness/volume). Inclusion not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast reported) and I7 (no significant whole-brain cluster peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (SnPM) with significant clusters (e.g., reduced GM in right frontal lobe and regional reductions in insula, IFG, ACC, precuneus) and refers to coordinates/tables produced with xjview. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and software (SPM8, SnPM), and participant demographics (male, ages reported). Thus it provides whole-brain voxelwise results with significant foci and sufficient methodological detail to contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or atlas-parcellation-only results, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between methamphetamine users and controls (meets I4 and I5) and reports participant demographics (meets I9). However, the study reports ROI-based, atlas-parcellation regional volumes aggregated per ROI (Talairach/MNI ROIs) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map with reported peak coordinates. It does not present any whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or significant peak coordinates (thus does not meet I6 or I7). Because the paper's results are derived from region-of-interest / atlas-parcellation analyses and lack voxelwise coordinate-based significant foci, it violates exclusion criteria E6 (atlas/parcellation-only results) and E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from this coordinate-based whole-brain meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical English-language MRI study of adolescent cannabis users vs controls and uses cortical thickness (surface-based) vertexwise analyses, meeting I4, I5 and I6. It also reports participant age/sex, substance-use details, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/software (FreeSurfer), satisfying I9. However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the significant whole-brain/vertexwise clusters; I7 (requirement that at least one significant whole-brain contrast yields reported peak coordinates) is not satisfied in the supplied content. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Because I7 is unmet, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded. Full text appears otherwise complete (methods/results/discussion present).

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses comparing opioid users (heroin, methadone-maintained, abstinent) with healthy controls and reports significant grey/white matter clusters with MNI coordinates; it assesses grey matter measures (grey matter probability/volume) and provides peak coordinates and correlations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion; supplemental images noted but core article content is present. Satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI study in English assessing GM differences), I5 (GM probability/volume), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts reported), I7 (significant clusters with coordinates reported), I8 (results in main text/tables), I9 (participant demographics and MRI details provided). No exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not parcellation-only, is empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing regular cannabis users to occasional users using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports significant clusters (with MNI coordinates summarized in tables) of decreased gray matter in multiple regions and voxelwise correlations with frequency of use. MRI acquisition (3T), preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), and participant demographics (male, ages provided) are reported. The study therefore provides qualifying whole-brain GM volume results suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis of cannabis-related GM differences.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol users vs controls and uses gray-matter volume measures (I4 and I5 satisfied) and reports participant age/sex and imaging/preprocessing details (I9 satisfied). However, the analyses are restricted to 24 a priori ROIs derived from the AAL and Neuromorphometrics atlases and use per-region mean gray-matter values (atlas parcellation/ROI approach). The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates, so it fails I6 (whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast) and I7 (reported significant peak coordinates). Because the only between-group results are ROI/atlas-parcellation based, exclusion criteria E5 and E6 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from this coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical MRI study (I4) using a cortical thickness measure (I5) and reports participant demographics and MRI details (I9). However, the analyses are based on FreeSurfer-derived atlas/parcellation ROIs and ROI-wise statistical tests (MANCOVA on predefined HASC ROIs). The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps nor peak coordinates from such analyses, so it fails the required whole-brain voxel/vertex map criterion (I6) and the requirement for significant whole-brain foci with coordinates (I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from a predefined atlas/parcellation rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise map).

The full text is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent smokers and nonsmokers using voxel-based morphometry (GMV) and reports significant whole-brain voxelwise results. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM regression showing a significant cluster in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex with peak MNI coordinates (x=6,y=30,z=-12) and cluster-size/statistical correction details. It also reports DTI voxelwise results for FA with coordinates. Participant age, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing, and statistical software are described. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Provided full text HTML is incomplete/truncated and lacks core article content (no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion). Therefore I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: whether this is an empirical MRI study in English (I4), whether grey-matter measures (I5) and whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates exist (I6, I7), nor whether results are available in tables/figures/supplement (I8) or participant/MRI details (I9). Because the full text is incomplete, inclusion cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E7) can be determined to apply based on the incomplete content.

Exclusion per E5: Although the study performed voxelwise whole-brain VBM analyses (I6) and is an empirical English-language MRI study reporting GM comparisons between cocaine users and controls (I4) using VBM measures (I5), the authors report that whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts were nonsignificant (no surviving clusters). The only significant structural finding reported is from a post-hoc spherical ROI analysis based on functional coordinates (ROI result: contralateral rACC F(1,50)=4.7, p=0.035). This means the paper does not provide any significant whole-brain voxelwise GM between-group peak coordinates (I7 not met), and its structural evidence depends on ROI analyses only. Therefore it must be excluded under E5. Also met: I8 and I9 (reporting of methodological and participant details).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (ANCOVA and paired tests) with family-wise error correction and significant GM and WM clusters (VBM results described; Table 3 referenced for peak coordinates and cluster sizes). The study measures gray matter volume, provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8), and reports regionally specific significant foci (insula, cingulate, etc.). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for whole-brain voxelwise GM differences with reported significant coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using surface-based morphometry (FreeSurfer) to compare cortical thickness and surface area between smokers, non-smoker MDD patients, and controls, and reports whole-brain vertexwise contrasts with significant clusters. However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any significant clusters nor include coordinate tables/figures in the content supplied. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (requirement for reported peak coordinates from whole-brain contrasts) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to controls and reports manual hippocampal volume differences, but it does not provide any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrasts or report peak coordinates. Exclusion: E5 applies because the study reports only region-of-interest (manual hippocampal tracings) analyses without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls), I5 (grey-matter measure: hippocampal volume), I9 (reported participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and methods). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast), I7 (no significant foci with reported peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

This paper is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to controls and reports gray-matter regional volumes (satisfies I4 and I5) and reports participant/MRI details (I9). However, the analyses are atlas-based regional (per-region) volume/parcellation measures rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps; no voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with peak coordinates is reported. Thus it fails I6 and I7. This violates exclusion criteria E6 (predefined atlas/parcellation per-region analyses) and E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical structural MRI study reporting whole-brain voxelwise (VBM) and vertexwise (SBM) analyses with significant clusters and peak coordinates and provides participant age/sex and MRI/software details (meets I5, I8, I9), it does NOT perform a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. The authors explicitly note a continuous-variable approach without a separate control group. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences between substance users and controls), I6 (whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls), and I7 (a whole-brain between-group contrast yielding significant foci with coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires between-group coordinates (users vs controls), this study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (uses voxel-based gray-matter volume measures via VBM), I6 (performed whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses across intracerebral voxels), I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (study does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls; analyses test correlations of substance use with gray matter across subjects rather than categorical user vs control group contrasts), I7 (the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for significant clusters in MNI/Talairach space; although regions are described, no coordinates are given in the supplied text and supplementary material is not provided here). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given the lack of a between-group substance-user vs control whole-brain contrast with reported coordinates, the study cannot contribute coordinate foci required for the planned coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This study reports empirical MRI measurements comparing alcohol-dependent individuals to controls (meets I4) and uses a grey-matter measure (hippocampal volume; meets I5). However, the analysis is ROI-based hippocampal volumetry (semi-automated hippocampal morphometry averaged bilaterally) and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise between-group contrast, nor does it report any peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast) and I7 (significant whole-brain foci with coordinates). As such it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI study comparing adolescent drinkers to no/low controls and reports regional cortical volume differences using FreeSurfer parcellations. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I5 (gray-matter volume/ cortical volume measures), and I9 (reports participant age/sex and processing software details). However, the paper does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps with peak coordinates; results are derived from atlas-based ROI/parcellation and regional slope comparisons (Desikan-Killiany ROIs) and therefore fail I6 and I7. Exclusion criteria triggered: E5 and E6 (study reports only ROI/parcellation-based between-group results, not qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with coordinates). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this coordinate-based whole-brain meta-analysis.

The paper is an empirical, English-language MRI study but reports resting-state functional MRI (ALFF and ReHo) results and uses voxel-based GM maps only as covariates. It does NOT present any whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts of grey-matter measures (volume/density/thickness) nor report peak coordinates for GM differences; the authors refer to a previous VBM report for details. Therefore it fails the key structural GM inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (participant demographics, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 (no reported whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise grey-matter between-group results with significant foci/coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete for the present article (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing heavy smokers (n=33) to never-smokers (n=22) that reports cerebellar grey-matter volume differences. It uses voxelwise VBM (SUIT toolbox) to analyze GM volume and reports a significant cluster in right Crus I with peak coordinates (−32, −71, −32) and multiple-comparison correction; results are presented in text, figures, and statistical thresholds. Participant demographics, dependence measures (FTND), scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, SUIT) are reported. The cerebellum-restricted voxelwise analysis reports coordinates and thus satisfies the review’s acceptance of sub-volume voxelwise maps. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study using cortical thickness (a surface-based grey-matter measure) comparing methamphetamine users and controls (meets I4 and I5). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing software (FreeSurfer) are reported (I9). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical map with surviving significant clusters and peak coordinates: the group comparison of cortical thickness was non-significant and no voxel/vertex coordinates or significant whole-brain foci are provided. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise results with coordinates are absent, the study effectively presents only global/regional (parcellation/GLMM) analyses rather than voxelwise/vertexwise results, invoking exclusion criteria E5 and E6. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it lacks qualifying whole-brain voxel/vertex coordinates and significant foci (fails I6/I7) and meets exclusion criteria E5 and E6.

This study investigates cortical thickness in children with fetal alcohol syndrome (prenatal alcohol exposure) and ADHD, comparing them to ADHD-only and healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (uses a grey-matter measure: cortical thickness) and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not compare substance-using participants vs controls — participants are not substance users but prenatally exposed children), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps are reported), and I7 (no significant whole-brain peak coordinates reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (results are reported as region-based/lobar and hemisphere averages rather than qualifying whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with coordinates). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot contribute coordinates to the voxelwise meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls reporting regional cerebellar gray-matter volumes derived from three atlas-based parcellation methods (Ceres, SUIT, Johns Hopkins). It therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison) and I5 (GM volume measures) and reports participant/MRI details (I9). However, the study does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps or peak coordinates (no VBM or voxelwise contrasts with x,y,z foci). All results are atlas parcellation/per-region average volumes. Thus it fails I6 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise contrast) and I7 (no reported significant voxel peak coordinates). This violates exclusion criterion E6 (only atlas/parcellation-based between-group results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The manuscript reports an empirical VBM study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and controls (whole-brain SPM2 analysis) and describes significant GM/WM clusters. However, the provided full text does not contain peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for any whole-brain significant clusters; such coordinates are required by inclusion criterion I7 and are likely in missing tables/figures. Therefore I cannot verify the presence of reported peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM measure via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I9 (reporting of key sample/MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no reported peak coordinates in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears incomplete (tables/figures likely omitted), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an empirical 1.5-T MRI study of alcoholic patients vs controls reporting GM volume deficits, satisfying I4 and I5. However, the abstract does not confirm that a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast was performed and does not report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so I6 and I7 cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are identifiable from the supplied content. Because the full article (methods and results with coordinate tables/figures) is not available, inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met/confirmable; therefore the study must be excluded pending full-text data.

This paper includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) results (whole-brain and ROI/SVC analyses) and reports peak coordinates for significant clusters, but the imaging comparisons reported are between obese subjects with vs without binge-eating and correlational analyses in healthy volunteers. Although the study enrolled abstinent methamphetamine and alcohol users for behavioral testing, it does not report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of substance users (any of the drug classes of interest) versus controls with reported peak coordinates. Therefore it fails the key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis: I4 (MRI study of substance users vs controls) and I6 (whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast for substance users vs controls). I7 (significant whole-brain foci for a substance-user vs control contrast) is also not fulfilled for substance-user contrasts. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (gray-matter measures reported) and I8 (coordinates/results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria from the review’s E-list were directly met.

This is an empirical MRI study of methamphetamine users reporting cortical thickness and subcortical volume differences (meets I4 and I5) and reports participant/MRI details (meets I9). However, the analyses are region-wise using FreeSurfer parcellation (mean thickness/volume over predefined cortical/subcortical ROIs) and MANCOVA/ANCOVAs across parcellation regions; no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical maps or peak coordinates are reported. Therefore the study does not provide qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates (does NOT meet I6 and I7). It thus violates exclusion criteria E5 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical structural MRI VBM comparison of nicotine-dependent smokers and controls (I4 met). It reports voxelwise DARTEL-based whole-brain GM and WM analyses and cluster-level significant differences (I6 met) and uses GM volume measures (I5 met). However, the provided full text does not include any reported peak coordinates (x,y,z) for significant clusters nor explicit statements that coordinate tables are available in the provided content. Inclusion criterion I7 (at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied based on the provided material. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a longitudinal voxelwise regression of a continuous alcohol-use index on within-subject GM volume change, not a between-group comparison of substance users versus controls. Although the study measures grey-matter volume change (I5 satisfied), it does not report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast comparing users and controls (I4 and I6 not met). The analyses were confined to a hippocampus/parahippocampus mask (ROI-restricted voxelwise analysis) rather than an unconstrained whole-brain between-group map; therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). It also does not provide a between-group contrast yielding peak coordinates for a users>controls or controls>users comparison (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I7. While it is an empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM (I4) using voxel-based and surface-based measures (I5), and it performed whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts (I6) with results and methods reported (I8,I9), all reported whole-brain contrasts yielded no significant clusters (the authors explicitly report null whole-brain results and ROI/shape analyses with no surviving corrected peaks). Therefore there are no significant peak coordinates to contribute to the coordinate-based meta-analysis (violates I7). No exclusion criteria E5–E7 directly apply (the paper did not report only ROI or atlas-parcellation results nor is it non-empirical), so exclusion is based on failure to satisfy I7. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a pathological postmortem volumetric study, not an in vivo MRI study, and therefore does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for voxelwise whole-brain MRI contrasts. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5 (the paper reports only ROI-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (it reports grey-matter measures — regional GM volumes) and I9 (reports participant/sample characteristics such as age, sex matching, alcohol/smoking history and MRI-related details are not applicable but demographic and tissue variables are reported). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (not an empirical MRI study — it uses postmortem histological/volumetric methods), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map or voxel coordinates reported), and I7 (no significant whole-brain foci/peak coordinates are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from this coordinate-based MRI meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study reports only region-wise volumetric comparisons derived from FreeSurfer segmentations (per-structure/cortical volumes) and does not present any voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps or peak coordinates. Therefore it violates criteria requiring whole-brain voxel/vertex results with reported coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (only ROI/region-wise analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas/parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical English MRI study comparing GM measures between exposed and controls), I5 (reports GM volume/cortical volume measures), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and processing software). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps with coordinates) and I7 (no significant foci with reported peak coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study cannot contribute coordinates required for the voxelwise coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients vs controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests with significant clusters (I4, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any whole-brain between-group contrasts. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates; that requirement is not met in the supplied text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered based on the available content. Therefore the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis unless a complete version with reported peak coordinates is supplied.

This is an empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing cocaine users and controls and reports GMV measures, but it does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of substance users vs controls with significant cluster coordinates. Between-group comparisons were performed using ROI-based extractions (rACC spheres) and reported ROI statistics; the authors explicitly state they did not report whole-brain group differences. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results without qualifying whole-brain coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I5 (GM volume measure), I9 (participant/MRI/preprocessing details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise results with reported significant foci). Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

Based on the provided full text, this is an empirical English MRI study of alcohol users vs controls using whole-brain VBM and subcortical segmentation. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study), I5 (reports GM density/volume measures), I6 (performed whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts), I8 (results described in text/figures), and I9 (reports age/sex and methodological details). This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent inpatients to healthy controls using surface-based cortical thickness measures. The authors performed a whole-brain, vertexwise/node-to-node analysis (Freesurfer surface reconstruction, SUMA/AFNI statistical testing) and report statistically significant clusters with Talairach peak coordinates. Participant, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing details are provided. Thus the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and none of the exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical, English VBM sMRI paper comparing substance users (cannabis and nicotine) to controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports significant clusters; however, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for any surviving whole-brain contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM volume via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I9 (reports participant demographics and MRI details). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no explicit peak coordinates for significant whole-brain clusters provided in the supplied text). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Therefore excluded because coordinate reporting required for coordinate-based meta-analysis (ALE) is absent in the provided full text.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrasts with reported peak coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas/parcellation regional volumes via FreeSurfer). This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing college-aged binge drinkers (alcohol users) to healthy volunteers. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 factorial) with cluster-level FWE correction and identifies significant clusters in multiple regions. It also reports peak MNI coordinates and statistics for at least one focus (ventral striatum MNI 12, -1.5, -10.5, Z=4.67, FWE P=0.002) and describes other whole-brain significant clusters. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 analyses (with MNI coordinates referenced in Table 2 and text), significant between-group clusters (OFC, DLPFC, temporal cortex, hippocampus), and details MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing, and participant demographics. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise whole-brain GM effects and provides reported peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study of heroin users vs controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and significant gray matter density (GMD) differences. However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any significant clusters. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one significant whole-brain contrast with reported peak coordinates. Because no coordinates are present in the supplied full text, the study cannot contribute coordinates for coordinate-based meta-analysis and therefore fails I7. The full text appears otherwise complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I9. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none.
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical English MRI study with structural MRI and substance users), I5 (grey-matter measure: VBM GM volume), I6 (voxelwise/whole-brain VBM analyses were performed across groups).
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I7 — the specific whole-brain contrast of substance users (alcohol-only group) versus controls did not yield any significant GM clusters with reported peak coordinates. The paper reports VBM group differences for schizophrenia (reduced left vlPFC) but does not provide significant whole-brain voxelwise coordinates for the alcohol user vs control comparison required by the meta-analysis. Therefore it cannot contribute coordinates to an ALE-style coordinate-based meta-analysis of alcohol-related GM differences. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter between heavy nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoker controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain VBM contrasts and provides peak coordinates in MNI space for significant clusters (GM reductions in cerebellum and other loci), satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain contrast with reported coordinates. Grey-matter measures (GM volume/density) are explicitly assessed. Results and methods (participants, ages/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software SPM5) are reported in full text. Although several findings were reported using small-volume correction (SVC) and some did not survive FDR/FWE at the whole-brain level, the study nonetheless provides voxelwise significant foci with coordinates and therefore meets inclusion criteria for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study comparing cigarette smokers to never-smokers and reporting whole-brain voxelwise grey-matter density differences. It meets I4 (empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I5 (grey-matter density via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrast), and I7 (at least one significant cluster with reported MNI coordinates: x = -34, y = 22, z = 14). Results are reported in main text/figures and methods include participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing software (SPM8, VBM8), satisfying I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E5), not an atlas-parcellation or multivariate-only analysis (E6), and not non-empirical (E7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). Although sample size is modest (16 smokers, 16 controls), all required criteria for inclusion in the voxelwise meta-analysis are satisfied.

This is an empirical, English-language optimized VBM MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent users vs matched controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray-matter (modulated GM volume) and significant between-group clusters (corrected p<0.05). The paper describes whole-brain SPM results and figures/tables (Table 2, Figure 1) with reported peak coordinates (a Talairach coordinate is explicitly given for right cerebellar white matter and GM clusters are listed in the paper’s result tables/figures), and reports multiple GM volume decreases (frontal, temporal, thalamus, bilateral cerebellum). Participant and MRI details are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing former heroin-dependent individuals to controls using voxel-based morphometry. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses with significant GM volume reductions (peak MNI coordinate provided, cluster size reported) and includes participant, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis details. Results are reported as whole-brain significant clusters with coordinates (satisfies requirement for significant foci). The study is not an ROI-only, atlas-parcellation, or non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for grey-matter voxelwise whole-brain results in an opioid-using sample.

This study is empirical, in English, and uses VBM to assess gray-matter volume in cocaine users vs controls (meets I4 and I5) and reports participant/sample/MRI details (meets I9). However, it does not report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast (substance users vs controls) with peak coordinates surviving whole-brain correction. The reported coordinates (BA24 x=-2,y=-18,z=40) derive from a whole-brain regression of N200 amplitude within controls and masked analyses, and the between-group comparison was performed on an extracted cluster value (post-hoc t-test), not as a voxelwise between-group SPM contrast with reported peaks. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because there is no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise result to contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using cortical thickness (a surface-based grey-matter measure acceptable per I5). The authors performed whole-cerebrum vertexwise analyses (FreeSurfer QDEC) comparing substance-using adolescents to controls (I6) and report a significant between-group cluster (controls > SUD) in left posterior cingulate/precuneus with a peak vertex coordinate provided (Talairach −5.6, −44.2, 30.0) (I7). Results/coordinates are presented in the main text/figure (I8). Participant, scanner, and preprocessing details are reported (I9). Although the significant whole-brain cluster arose in an exploratory model covarying IQ and whole-brain thickness (not the primary age+IQ model, which was null), the study nonetheless reports a qualifying whole-brain significant voxel/vertex-wise contrast with coordinates. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM2) comparing bipolar adolescents with cannabis use disorders to bipolar adolescents without CUD. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and peak Talairach coordinates (GM volume and density differences). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise whole-brain GM analyses of cannabis users vs controls.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of nicotine users vs controls that reports cortical thickness (surface-based) and subcortical volume comparisons (I4 and I5 satisfied). The paper performed whole-brain vertexwise cortical thickness analyses using FreeSurfer Qdec (I6 satisfied). However, the full text as provided does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for any whole-brain between-group contrasts or correlations, and no tables/figures with coordinates are included; therefore criterion I7 (reporting of significant foci with coordinates) is not met. Because I7 is required for inclusion, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are otherwise triggered by the content provided. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is set to false.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing a substance-using group (first-time DWI offenders, primarily alcohol-related) to non-DWI controls. The study uses a surface-based grey-matter measure (cortical thickness) and conducts whole-brain vertexwise analyses using SurfStat, reporting significant clusters with MNI peak coordinates in the right dorsal posterior cingulate cortex (and other clusters). It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I5 (cortical thickness accepted), I6 (whole-brain vertexwise statistical map), I7 (significant foci with reported coordinates), I8 (results reported clearly), and I9 (participant and MRI details reported). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). While the study is an empirical English-language MRI study of prenatal alcohol exposure vs controls and uses surface-based and volumetric gray-matter measures (meeting I4 and I5), the provided content does not confirm that a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with reported peak coordinates was performed and yielded significant clusters. I cannot verify I6 (whole-brain voxel/vertex map with coordinates) or I7 (at least one significant cluster with peak coordinates). Because those required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the available text, the study must be excluded pending full-text review.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps with stereotactic peak coordinates. Instead, it reports manual parcellation-based regional (64-unit) volumetric/ROI analyses and a priori region comparisons without reporting voxel coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results) and E6 (between-group results derived from atlas/parcellation units rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English-language MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I5 (reports grey-matter volume measures), and I9 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast with reported coordinates) and I7 (no significant voxel/vertex peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results are derived from an atlas-based parcellation of 34 FreeSurfer regions rather than from a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map) and E5 (only region-of-interest/parcellation-based analyses reported with no qualifying voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain results or coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English-language structural MRI study) and I5 (uses a grey-matter measure: cortical thickness). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps reported) and I7 (no significant whole-brain foci with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space reported). Although the paper reports comprehensive regionwise cortical thickness differences and provides methodological details (ages, sex distribution, 3.0T scanner, FreeSurfer v5.1), it lacks voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrasts and reported peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus non-user controls. Specifically: Inclusion criteria met: I5 (uses grey-matter surface-based measures such as cortical thickness) and I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls — only compares early- vs late-onset users within a user sample), I6 (no whole-brain substance-user vs control voxelwise/vertexwise contrast), and I7 (no qualifying significant user-vs-control foci with reported coordinates). Exclusion criteria: none of E5–E7 apply, but failure to meet I4/I6/I7 is sufficient for exclusion from the meta-analysis focused on user vs control GM differences. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of adolescent alcohol use vs non-using co-twins and reports grey-matter measures (regional volumes and cortical thickness) processed with FreeSurfer on a 3T scanner (meets I4, I5, I9). However, analyses are based on selected a priori regional/parcellation measures (FreeSurfer-derived region volumes/thicknesses) and linear mixed models/co-twin comparisons, not on whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps with reported peak coordinates. The paper does not report any voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrasts or peak (x,y,z) coordinates. Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criteria E5 and E6 (ROI/parcellation-based results only). Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: E5, E6; Inclusion met: I4, I5, I9; Inclusion not met: I6, I7.

The study is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study reporting whole-brain GM density differences between cannabis-using adolescent-onset schizophrenia patients and non-using patients (and reporting schizophrenia vs controls). It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I5 (uses GM density/volume via VBM), I6 (reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, e.g., CAN+ve vs CAN−ve), and I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength and preprocessing/software). However, the provided full text does not report peak voxel coordinates (x,y,z) for the significant GM clusters; criterion I7 requires at least one whole-brain contrast to yield significant clusters with reported peak coordinates. Because I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text, the study cannot contribute coordinate-level data to the meta-analysis and must be excluded. The full text appears otherwise complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter between substance users (heroin and cocaine) and healthy controls. Whole-brain voxelwise ANCOVA analyses were performed (SPM5) with cluster-corrected results reported; the methods state anatomical regions were converted to Talairach coordinates, indicating reported peak coordinates for significant clusters. The substances studied (heroin = opioid, cocaine = stimulant) fall within the meta-analysis pharmacological classes of interest. Core article content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and reports significant whole-brain foci. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and age-/sex-matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses (group ANCOVA and contrasts of patients vs controls) and lists significant clusters with peak coordinates (see Table 3 and Figure 3), satisfying the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast yielding significant foci. Grey-matter measures (local gray matter volume) are reported. Voxelwise results are provided in tables/figures and methods/reporting includes participant demographics, MRI acquisition and preprocessing details. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients to healthy controls (HR and non-HR). It uses high-resolution T1-weighted images analyzed with CAT12/SPM12 and reports whole-brain voxel/vertexwise contrasts (ANOVA and t-tests) thresholded at p<0.05 FDR with significant clusters. The study measures cortical thickness (an accepted grey-matter metric for this review) and reports significant between-group clusters and associated whole-brain results presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) subjects to healthy controls and problem gamblers and finds significant regional GM reductions. However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the significant clusters (no coordinate tables or values are present in the supplied content). Inclusion criterion I7 requires that at least one whole-brain contrast yields significant clusters with reported peak coordinates. Therefore the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM volume/density measure via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I9 (reporting of sample and MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no reported peak coordinates in supplied text). No exclusion criteria (E5-E7) apply based on the provided content. Full text appears complete for core sections, but coordinate reporting is absent in the provided material.

Exclusion due to lack of qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical maps with reported peak coordinates.
