Study is an empirical VBM study of cocaine-dependent individuals vs controls (stimulant class) and reports voxelwise gray-matter analyses and coordinates for within-group regression effects, so I4 and I5 are satisfied. However, the paper reports no significant between-group gray-matter differences (no surviving clusters in the group contrast after ROI/SVC correction), and thus the required whole-brain between-group contrast yielding at least one significant peak is absent. The significant coordinates reported are from within-group correlations (severity vs GM) rather than a substance-users vs controls contrast. This violates inclusion criterion I7 and effectively falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-restricted analyses with no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Empirical voxel-based morphometry study in English comparing nicotine-dependent smokers vs controls; reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant clusters and MNI coordinates (thalamus, amygdala, insula, etc.); includes GM volume/density measures, participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical methods. No exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study assessing grey-matter differences (cortical thickness) between cocaine users and controls and thus meets I4 and I5. However, the analyses are ROI/parcellation-based (Desikan–Killiany atlas averages of six frontal ROIs and per-region subcortical volumes via MAGeTbrain) rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps. The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise between-group contrasts with peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and violates exclusion criteria E5 (ROI-only results) and E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). No whole-brain coordinate-based foci are available to contribute to the coordinate-based meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English VBM study of heroin-dependent men vs controls reporting GMV differences (right DLPFC) with MNI coordinates. However, the only significant GMV finding was obtained using small-volume correction within an a priori DLPFC ROI; the paper states that other whole-brain GMV differences were nonsignificant. Per inclusion criterion I7, a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast must yield at least one significant cluster (with reported coordinates); findings that are significant only after ROI/small-volume correction do not satisfy I7. Therefore this study must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI/SVC results with no qualifying whole-brain significant clusters). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI GM study), I5 (GM volume measure via VBM), I6 (performed voxelwise whole-brain contrast), I8 (reports coordinates/figures), I9 (reports participant/MRI details). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no significant whole-brain clusters). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing occasional stimulant (ATS and cocaine) users to matched controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (LME) and voxelwise regressions within users, yielding multiple significant clusters (striatum, vmPFC, insula, cerebellum, parietal) with peak coordinates reported (and/or provided in supplemental materials). The manuscript details MRI field strength (3T), acquisition and preprocessing (FSL-VBM, segmentation, modulation, smoothing), statistical methods, and participant demographics/substance measures. Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM study), I5 (GM volume/density via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (significant clusters with reported peaks), I8 (results available in main/supplemental materials), and I9 (reporting of key methodological and participant details). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing amphetamine-dependent subjects to controls using surface-based cortical thickness measures (satisfies I4, I5). The analysis is vertexwise across the whole cortical mantle (satisfies I6) and voxelwise/vertexwise results are shown in figures (I8); participant and acquisition details are reported (I9). However, although they report significant whole-brain group differences for the subgroup of amphetamine users with heavy alcohol use, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (MNI or Talairach) for any significant whole-brain clusters. Per inclusion criterion I7, a qualifying whole-brain contrast must yield at least one significant cluster with reported peak coordinates. Because I7 is not met, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing 33 heavy cannabis users with 42 controls. It reports between-group voxelwise analyses and significant grey-matter differences (increased anterior cerebellar GM in users) and voxelwise within-group correlations in hippocampus and amygdala related to use/dependence. The methods describe whole-brain VBM processing (SPM8/VBM8), thresholds for whole-brain and ROI analyses, and reporting of results (figures/tables implied). Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Therefore it meets criteria I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I5 (GM volume via VBM), I6 (voxelwise/whole-brain VBM contrasts performed), I7 (significant foci reported), I8 (results available in figures/tables), and I9 (participant/MRI details reported). Confidence is slightly reduced because exact peak coordinates are not visible in the provided excerpt (likely in omitted tables/figures), but the paper clearly presents voxelwise significant clusters. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical MRI investigation of prenatal stimulant (cocaine) and tobacco exposure and reports cortical thickness and subcortical volume differences (meets I4 and I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps with peak coordinates; analyses are based on FreeSurfer-derived region/parcellation measures (DLPFC, VMPFC, averaged subcortical volumes) and ROI-style comparisons. No MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise/vertexwise maps are provided, so I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Therefore the study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation results (E5 and E6).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing methamphetamine (stimulant) users to controls and reporting whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray-matter density (meets I4, I5, I6). However, in the provided full text the required whole-brain significant peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) are not present—the manuscript text contains placeholders (e.g., “( , and )”) and no tables/figures/supplementary coordinate listings were provided. Inclusion criterion I7 (reported peak coordinates for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast) therefore cannot be verified from the supplied content. Because I7 is mandatory, the study cannot be included on the basis of the provided full text. fulltext_incomplete is set because critical information (coordinates/tables/figures) appears missing from the supplied article copy.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol users (alcohol use disorder/abusers) and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts for grey matter and white matter, with statistically significant clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., left OFC x=-28,y=64,z=-4; mPFC coordinates provided). GM volume/density measures are assessed. MRI field strength, preprocessing (SPM5, VBM5), and participant details are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4–I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, atlas-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is an empirical MRI study that reports regional (inferior and superior frontal) gray-matter volumes and finds smaller inferior frontal GM in cocaine users, so it meets I4 and I5. However, the volumetric analyses are region-of-interest (anatomically defined frontal masks) rather than whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise GM analyses; the only voxelwise analyses reported are on DTI fractional anisotropy (white-matter microstructure), not on gray-matter measures, and no voxelwise GM contrast with peak coordinates is reported. Therefore the study does not provide the required whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise GM contrast nor any reported significant peak coordinates, failing I6 and I7. As a result it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain GM results) and cannot be included in the coordinate-based GM meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult smokers (nicotine users) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (SPM8 VBM two-sample t-test, whole-brain, FWE-corrected) and reports significant GM volume differences (decreased left ACC, increased left putamen). The paper describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses and indicates results/figures and supplementary material where peak results are presented. Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I5 (GM volume measure), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (reports significant clusters), I8 (results available in figures/supplementary materials), and I9 (reports participant and MRI details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Supplementary tables/figures likely contain coordinates per the manuscript; inclusion is based on the presented whole-brain VBM results and statement that coordinates are available in supplement/figures.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of cannabis users vs controls that reports voxelwise whole-brain VBM results with significant clusters and peak coordinates (MNI) and also provides regional volume and shape analyses. The paper explicitly performed whole-brain VBM, lists significant foci in tables/figures (with coordinates), and reports participant demographics, scanner details (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4–I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-only, and not non-empirical). The methods describe a whole-brain voxelwise analysis (VBM2/SPM2) and the results report significant clusters in prefrontal, supplementary motor, and cingulate cortices, referenced to Table 1 and Figure 1 (voxelwise whole-brain contrast). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it satisfies whole-brain voxelwise GM-volume criteria and yields significant foci; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of prenatal alcohol exposure reporting grey-matter volumes (cortical and deep GM) and regionwise comparisons using FreeSurfer segmentation. It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM volume measures), and I9 (reports age/sex and MRI field strength). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps with peak coordinates; results are per-region volumes/segmentation (atlas/parcellation) and ROI-style comparisons. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with reported coordinates). As such it violates exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI/parcellation results with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from a predefined atlas/parcellation rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise map). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

The study used atlas-based regional averages (a 1,024-ROI parcellation) and multivariate classification (SVM-RFE) as its primary between-group analysis; it does not report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with surviving significant clusters and peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English sMRI study comparing substance users and controls), I5 (grey-matter measure = GM volume), I9 (reports participant demographics and MRI/scanner details). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast reported), I7 (no reported significant whole-brain peak coordinates from such a contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derive from an atlas parcellation and multivariate classifier rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map) and E5 (only ROI/parcellation-based findings and classifier-based results; no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this voxelwise coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study reports manual ROI grey-matter volumetry (temporal lobe, superior temporal gyrus, hippocampus/amygdala) and participant details (satisfies I4, I5, I9). However it does NOT provide a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast of grey-matter measures with significant peak coordinates; the only voxelwise significant coordinates reported are for diffusion measures (FA and ADC), not grey-matter volume. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical 3T structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent subjects vs controls that performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBM and VBM) comparing grey-matter measures. It meets inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM measures: TBM/Jacobian and VBM GM volume/density), and I6 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts were conducted using SPM8). However, all voxelwise whole-brain contrasts reported in the full text yielded no significant clusters (the authors explicitly report no surviving voxels at FWE-corrected P<0.05), so inclusion criterion I7 (at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it provides null whole-brain voxelwise results and thus contributes no coordinates to the meta-analysis.

Full text lacks sufficient reporting of peak coordinates for whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts. The study is an empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users and controls (meets I4, I5) and reports performing whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I6). However, the provided full text only includes MNI coordinates for hippocampal small-volume-corrected results and a within-group covariate result; it does not provide peak coordinates for the whole-brain between-group GM contrasts in the main text (these appear to be in missing tables/figures). This study examines adolescents with prenatal cocaine exposure (PCE) versus non-cocaine-exposed (NCE) controls, not current substance users versus controls; therefore it does not meet the review’s primary population/comparison requirement (I4). However, in the provided full text there are no explicit peak coordinates (x,y,z) reported for the significant clusters, so criterion I7 (reported peak coordinates for whole-brain significant foci) is not demonstrably met from the content supplied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered by the provided content. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of prenatal alcohol exposure vs controls reporting subcortical gray-matter volume differences using FreeSurfer regional parcellation. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance-exposed subjects and controls), I5 (reports gray-matter volume measures including subcortical GM), I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strengths, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps nor peak coordinates; analyses are based on atlas/parcellation region volumes (FreeSurfer labels). Therefore the study is not eligible for coordinate-based meta-analysis and is excluded. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The manuscript is an empirical English-language VBM study of heroin (opioid) users vs controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant GM volume reductions, but the provided full text does NOT include peak coordinate reporting (x,y,z) for the significant clusters. Although the main text refers to supplementary data, those supplementary tables/coordinate lists are not present in the supplied full text. Inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I8 are satisfied (empirical MRI VBM study; GM volume measure; whole-brain voxelwise analysis; main text indicates results/supplement exist). Fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study of methamphetamine (a stimulant) users versus drug-naïve controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons with significant clusters. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM volume via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI/Talairach) for the significant clusters in the material supplied. Because I7 requires at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates and those coordinates are not present in the supplied full text, the study cannot be confirmed to qualify. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered by the available content. The supplied full text may be incomplete (tables or figures that could contain coordinates are not included).

This is an empirical, English-language 3T MRI voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study comparing grey matter volume between detoxified alcohol-dependent patients (n=22 with relapse data) and 22 matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain VBM group contrasts (patients vs controls; relapsers vs abstainers) with significant clusters surviving whole-brain FWE cluster correction and refers to Supplemental Table S1/S2 for complete results, consistent with reporting of peak coordinates in supplementary material. The study therefore provides voxelwise whole-brain evidence of GM differences using GM volume measures. It is not an ROI-only, atlas-parcellation, or non-empirical paper. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and supplementary results are explicitly referenced. Hence all inclusion criteria I4–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply.

This empirical structural MRI VBM study reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing adolescents with BD who later developed substance use problems (CRAFFTHIGH) versus those who did not (CRAFFTLOW). Significant GMV clusters with MNI coordinates are reported (OFC, rPFC, dlPFC, insula, temporopolar). The paper provides details on participants (age/sex), MRI field strength, preprocessing, and statistical software. Although MRI was acquired prior to substance exposure and groups are defined by later substance use, the manuscript nonetheless implements a whole-brain voxelwise contrast of substance-users (at follow-up) vs controls and reports peak coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: a potential conceptual caveat is that ‘users’ were not actively using at scan time, which may affect comparability with studies scanning current users, but this does not violate the stated criteria.

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI comparison of cannabis users vs controls and reports voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and SBM) with significant SBM clusters. However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the significant whole-brain clusters; inclusion criterion I7 requires reported peak coordinates for at least one significant whole-brain contrast. Therefore I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, but I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete regarding main sections, but coordinate reporting required by the meta-analysis is absent in the provided content, so the study cannot contribute usable coordinate foci and must be excluded.

Full text is not accessible (paywalled) and provided content is limited to title, metadata, and purchase notice. Cannot verify core methods or results. Therefore I cannot confirm required inclusion criteria: I4 (empirical MRI assessing GM differences) cannot be confirmed; I5 (GM measure type) not confirmed; I6 (whole-brain voxel/vertexwise contrast with coordinates) not confirmed; I7 (significant foci with reported coordinates) not confirmed; I8/I9 not verifiable. No exclusion criteria (E5-E7) are demonstrably met from the available content. Because the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be reliably assessed for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical MRI investigation of AUD vs controls using FreeSurfer vertexwise (surface-based) and volumetric analyses, and reports significant whole-brain vertexwise clusters in cortical thickness/GM volume (e.g., left fusiform, right parahippocampal gyrus, left temporal pole). However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables for the significant whole-brain clusters, which is required by I7. Therefore the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis based on the available content. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study comparing users vs controls), I5 (grey-matter measures including cortical thickness and volume), I6 (whole-brain vertexwise/voxelwise analyses performed). Inclusion criterion not met / not verifiable from provided text: I7 (no reported peak coordinates in the provided full text). Full text appears to omit the coordinate tables/explicit peak coordinates, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study used deformation-based morphometry on longitudinal MRI data of alcoholic women vs controls and reports whole-brain Jacobian maps and region-based statistical tests. However, the meta-analysis requires whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts of grey-matter measures with at least one significant cluster reported as peak coordinates. Although voxelwise Jacobian (log-Jacobian) maps are computed and demographics are reported, the paper’s primary between-group statistical results are reported as region-integrated tests over an 18-region segmentation (atlas parcellation) and the manuscript does not provide peak (x,y,z) coordinates for any whole-brain significant grey-matter clusters. The reported significant effects focus on ventricles, CSF and white matter rather than grey-matter clusters with coordinates. Therefore the study cannot contribute coordinate-based grey-matter foci required by this meta-analysis and is excluded (exclusion E6). Included criteria met: I6 (voxelwise maps created) and I9 (demographics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (explicit grey-matter volume results), I5 (use of grey-matter specific measures reported as results), I7 (no reported peak coordinates for significant clusters), I8 (no coordinates in tables/figures/supplement).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls (substance users vs controls). It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patients < controls and genotype effects) with significant clusters and peak MNI coordinates, uses standard VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) and a 3T scanner, and provides participant demographics and substance-use/relapse data. Therefore it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI study), I5 (GM volume via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (significant foci with coordinates), I8 (results reported in main text/tables/figures), and I9 (reports age/sex, scanner and preprocessing). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not atlas/parcellation-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to assess gray-matter volume differences between cocaine-dependent patients and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (age-adjusted ANCOVA) with significant clusters and peak MNI coordinates (left striatum: −5,2,−1; right supramarginal gyrus: 50,−60,32) and cluster statistics. Participant characteristics (age, sex, substance use history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5 toolbox) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Recommended inclusion in the meta-analysis of substance-user vs. control GM differences for stimulants (cocaine).

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing frequent cannabis users and controls (measures: grey matter density), satisfying that it is an empirical English MRI study of GM (I4) and uses GM density measures (I5). However, the VBM results were restricted to a small-volume/small-ROI analysis of the (para)hippocampal region (semi-automatic small volume correction) and yielded no significant between-group clusters or peak coordinates. Therefore the paper does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise contrast with at least one significant focus (fails I6/I7). Because the only structural between-group testing was confined to an ROI/SVC and produced null results, exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This MRI study of chronic alcoholics reports cortical gray and white matter volume deficits using regional volumetric analyses (six cortical regions) comparing alcoholic groups to controls, satisfying inclusion criteria I4 (empirical English MRI study) and I5 (grey-matter measure: GM volume). However, the paper does not present a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain between-group statistical map with reported peak coordinates, and instead reports regional/ROI volumetry (no voxel coordinates provided), thus failing inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the provided content appears to be only abstract/metadata rather than the complete article (methods/results/discussion not fully present), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Given these points, the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray-matter tissue density between abstinent cocaine users and non-drug-using controls using voxel-based morphometry (satisfies I4 and I5). Analyses were performed as voxelwise SPM contrasts within anatomically defined small-volume templates (a sub-volume voxelwise map), and the paper reports significant clusters and peak coordinates for at least some contrasts (e.g., white-matter correlation peaks) and indicates coordinate-based results/figures for gray-matter clusters (satisfies I6, I7, and I8). Although analyses used small-volume correction rather than an unconstrained whole-brain search, the review protocol accepts anatomically confined voxelwise maps with reported coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria were met (e.g., not solely an ROI atlas-parcellation or non-empirical).

The study is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing substance users and controls (I4) and uses gray matter volume measures (I5). It performs whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses (I6) and reports significant clusters (FWE cluster-corrected) and methodological details (age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) (I9). However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for the significant whole-brain clusters, nor tables/figures/supplementary coordinate lists in the supplied content; inclusion criterion I7 (presence of at least one significant whole-brain contrast with reported peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied. I8 (acceptability of coordinates in tables/figures/supplement) is also not met based on the supplied full text. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 (and I8) are not satisfied in the provided full text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis as presented here. Full text appears to lack coordinate tables/figures, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM8/VBM8) with family-wise error-corrected significant clusters (text references Table 3 and Figure 2) and at least one explicit MNI coordinate is provided in the full text. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for voxelwise whole-brain GM comparisons and reports significant peak foci with coordinates.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing chronic cocaine users (stimulant class) with healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess grey matter volume. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (permutation-based cluster inference) and provides significant cluster results with MNI coordinates (e.g., orbitofrontal cortex, caudate, insula, middle temporal gyrus). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (FSLVBM/FSL tools) and participant demographics/substance-use details are reported. Results are not ROI-only or atlas-parcellation only. Therefore it satisfies whole-brain voxelwise reporting of significant grey-matter differences and supplies coordinate foci suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical structural MRI study assessing cortical volumes (meets I4 and I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates; analyses are based on FreeSurfer-derived region/parcellation volumes and ROI/GLM comparisons without voxelwise coordinates. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. This violates exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas/parcellation region averages rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (and thus I8/I9 are moot). Exclusion criteria applied: E5, E6. Consequently the paper should be excluded from the voxelwise coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Although this paper includes voxel-based morphometry and reports significant gray-matter correlations with a behavioral parameter (α) in healthy volunteers with MNI coordinates, it does not report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts comparing substance users (alcohol- or stimulant-dependent groups) versus controls. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain between-group GM comparison with surviving significant clusters and reported peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (empirical MRI study reporting GM differences between substance users and controls), I6 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise evidence), and I7 (at least one significant between-group focus with coordinates). The study does meet criteria I5 (uses gray-matter VBM measures) and I8 (reports whole-brain coordinates for its reported correlation results) and provides participant details (I9). Because the required between-group whole-brain contrasts are absent, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls assessing hippocampal gray-matter volume using VBM-derived hippocampal ROI measures. It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls) and I5 (uses gray-matter volume measures). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with surviving significant clusters and peak coordinates: the morphometric analysis is confined to hippocampal ROI integration (no whole-brain significant foci or coordinates are provided). Thus it fails I6 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result) and I7 (no reported significant whole-brain foci with coordinates). Per the review exclusion rules, this is effectively an ROI-only morphometric report and meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls, with significant clusters reported and peak coordinates in MNI space. It uses an empirical human MRI sample, assesses grey-matter volume (VBM), performs whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM2), and reports significant foci with coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or atlas-parcellation-only approach).

This is an empirical MRI study reporting cortical morphometry (volumes, surface area, thickness) and group comparisons; however all between-group results are derived from FreeSurfer atlas-based regional parcellation (per-region averages/composites) and univariate ROI statistics. The paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps nor does it provide peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) from a whole-brain contrast. Therefore it does not meet the required whole-brain voxel/vertex evidence and significant-coordinate reporting for inclusion in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This study reports empirical human structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) comparing heroin (opioid) abusers and healthy controls, meeting the review focus on substance-related GM alterations. Methods detail whole-brain VBM analyses (FSL-VBM) with modulation and smoothing, and results report significant whole-brain group effects and genotype×group interactions with AlphaSim-corrected clusters. The manuscript explicitly references Supplementary Tables S7 and S8 for imaging results (implying reported peak coordinates in tables/ supplementation) and describes MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant age/sex. Therefore it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM differences), I5 (GMV measure), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (significant clusters reported; coordinates indicated as available in supplementary tables), I8 (results available in supplementary materials), and I9 (key participant/MRI/method details provided). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain analyses comparing nicotine-dependent smokers (n=80) to matched controls (n=80). The methods report voxelwise SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing and whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster-level inference (p<=0.001, FWE cluster-corrected p<0.025) and significant clusters described in results (thalamus, cerebellum, putamen, parahippocampus) and figures/tables. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no atlas-parcellation-only, and it is empirical human MRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis users and non-users using whole-brain vertexwise (surface-based) analyses (FreeSurfer cortical thickness) and subcortical volumes. The paper reports significant whole-brain vertexwise clusters with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics (e.g., cluster locations and MNIX/MNIY/MNIZ values), satisfying the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast with reported peak coordinates. Grey-matter measures include cortical thickness and subcortical volumes. Participant demographics, MRI acquisition and preprocessing (FreeSurfer) and statistical methods are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing bipolar I patients with prior alcohol use disorder (BD-AUD) to bipolar patients without AUD (BD-nonAUD) and to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 VBM), provides MNI peak coordinates and cluster sizes for significant between-group contrasts (BD-AUD vs BD-nonAUD: left medial frontal gyrus and right anterior cingulate gyrus; coordinates and t/k values reported), and describes MRI field strength (1.5 T) and preprocessing/software details. The grey-matter measure is VBM GM volume. Although ROI small-volume correction was applied to predefined ROIs, the study reports voxelwise peak coordinates from between-group contrasts rather than only ROI-average or parcellation results. The full text includes methods, results and discussion and is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because the whole-brain vertexwise analyses did not yield any surviving significant clusters with reported peak coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (study reports ROI results but has no qualifying whole-brain results surviving correction). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I5 (uses cortical thickness, an acceptable surface-based GM measure), I6 (performed whole-brain vertexwise/vertex-based analyses), I9 (reports participant age/sex, substance use details, MRI field strength, and processing software). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (the required whole-brain contrast did not yield at least one significant cluster with reported peak coordinates—vertex-wise clusters did not survive clusterwise correction and no whole-brain significant foci with coordinates are provided). Full text appears complete. Given I7 is not satisfied, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the voxelwise meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study reports ROI-based analyses (left lateral OFC and hippocampus) using FreeSurfer-derived regional volumes and tests associations with drinking, but it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise between-group contrasts nor report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain coordinate-based results for inclusion in an ALE-style meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing alcohol-dependent patients to healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM8/DARTEL) with significant clusters (medial frontal, lateral prefrontal, parietal-occipital) and provides coordinates and cluster statistics (converted to Talairach), satisfying the requirement for reported peak coordinates. Grey-matter measures are modulated gray matter volumes (voxelwise), and participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI acquisition and preprocessing details are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (alcohol is one target drug class). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content.

This is an empirical MRI study of smokers vs. controls using cortical thickness (FreeSurfer) and reports demographic/MRI details, but all between-group analyses are reported as region-wise averages over FreeSurfer/Desikan-Killiany ROIs (34 bilateral regions) and composite ROI measures. The manuscript does not present a voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain statistical map, nor does it report peak coordinates. Therefore it does not meet I6 or I7 and violates the meta-analysis exclusion criteria for ROI/parcellation-only results. Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study in English comparing chronic cocaine users vs controls and reports gray-matter volume measures (VBM) with subject/sample and MRI details (meets I4, I5, I9). However, the only significant gray-matter finding reported survived correction within an a priori ROI (VMPFC); the authors state that outside the ROIs no gray-matter reductions survived whole-brain correction. Therefore there are no qualifying whole-brain significant voxelwise between-group clusters with reported peak coordinates to contribute to an ALE-style meta-analysis. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only surviving results). Inclusion criteria not met: I6/I7 (no surviving whole-brain significant voxelwise foci reported). Full text appears complete.

This study reports global gray-matter measures (total cortical GM and GM/ICV ratio) derived from tissue-segmentation and group-level regression analyses between alcohol-dependent participants and controls, but it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps or peak coordinates. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results with reported significant cluster coordinates. Exclusion(s) met: E5. Inclusion(s) met: I4 (empirical MRI study of GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I5 (reports GM volume measure). Inclusion(s) not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map reported), I7 (no significant cluster foci with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5, E6. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I9. (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6, I7. Rationale: This empirical English-language MRI study compares grey-matter measures between adolescent cannabis users and controls and reports regional cortical volume/surface-area/thickness measures (satisfying I4 and I5) and provides participant and MRI details (I9).
