This empirical, English-language MRI study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. It reports a whole-brain voxelwise between-group analysis with a significant cluster in left inferior frontal gyrus (MNI -48, 11, 10; Z=5.11; p=0.005, FWE-corrected), satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain peak coordinate. The paper provides participant age/sex, drinking history, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, atlas-parcellation-only results, non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E6 (results derived from an atlas parcellation rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map). Specifically, cortical thickness was averaged within AAL regions for all statistical analyses and volumes were analyzed by regional (FreeSurfer) segmentations, with no voxelwise or vertexwise between-group statistical maps reported and no peak coordinates provided. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical human MRI study comparing alcohol-exposed subjects to controls) and I5 (grey-matter measure included cortical thickness/volumes). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast reported) and I7 (no significant whole-brain foci with reported peak coordinates). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical MRI study of methamphetamine (stimulant) users vs controls and reports cortical thickness and subcortical volumes (meets I4, I5, I9). However, the paper does not report any voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain between-group statistical maps with reported peak coordinates. Analyses are presented as global or lobar/region-averaged measures (FreeSurfer-derived regional summaries) and post-hoc regional correlations, with no significant whole-brain clusters or coordinates provided. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because the study’s between-group results are effectively region-based/parcellation or ROI-style analyses with no qualifying whole-brain coordinate results, it meets exclusion criteria E5 and E6. Excluded for lacking whole-brain voxel/vertex coordinates required by the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxelwise tensor-based morphometry (TBM) comparing prenatally alcohol-exposed children to controls (so it meets I4 and I6), the full text does not report any peak coordinates (MNI or Talairach) for significant voxelwise clusters required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7. In addition, the TBM results describe 'brain tissue' (gray and white matter and CSF) rather than a clear voxelwise grey-matter (GM-only) measure, so I5 is at best ambiguous and likely not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Given lack of reported coordinates (and uncertain GM-specific voxelwise contrasts), this study cannot contribute coordinates to the intended coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I7: the provided full text describes significant whole-brain voxelwise VBM results but does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the significant clusters in the material provided. The paper does satisfy I4 (empirical English MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I5 (reports GM volume/density measures), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts with significant clusters), I8 (results presented in tables/figures), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5,E6,E7) apply. Full text appears complete for intro/methods/results/discussion, but because coordinates are not present in the provided content, it cannot contribute coordinate foci to the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical English-language MRI study measuring cortical gray matter volumes in alcohol-dependent long-term abstinent subjects vs controls (meets I4, I5) and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I9). However, the analysis is ROI / atlas-based (lobar and Brodmann-area aggregation) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map. No voxel coordinates or peak foci are reported from a whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails the whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise requirement (I6) and the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported coordinates (I7). This also triggers exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise map). Full text appears complete. Consequently, the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study reports manual ROI-based MRI measures of frontal and temporal lobe volumes (gray and white matter) from a contiguous seven-slice slab and presents group comparisons and correlations, but it does not perform or report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical contrast with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain voxelwise evidence criteria (I6) and the requirement for significant foci with reported coordinates (I7). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry assessing gray-matter volume differences between former regular substance users (FRUs) and former light users (FLUs). The paper reports voxelwise ROI and exploratory whole-brain analyses with significant clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., reported peak at −27, −12, −4 and multiple whole-brain clusters), satisfying the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast with significant foci. Core methods (MRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical software) and participant/substance-use details are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Although the “control” group consists of former light users rather than drug-naive participants, the inclusion criteria require a between-group voxelwise contrast and significant coordinates, which this study provides.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing active heavy drinkers to light-drinking controls (I4). It quantifies grey-matter measures (lobar GM volumes via probabilistic segmentation and focal GM/WM contraction via deformation tensor morphometry) satisfying I5. The paper performs voxelwise deformation-morphometry whole-brain analyses (I6) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (I9). However, although the authors state that voxelwise statistical maps and some clusters survived corrected thresholds and illustrate results in figures, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for any significant cluster. Because inclusion criterion I7 (at least one whole-brain contrast yielding ≥1 significant cluster with reported peak coordinates) is not met, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered by the content provided.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study that reports voxelwise whole-brain GMV results (including reported peak coordinates) and details on participants, MRI field strength, and preprocessing. However, it does not present a whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrast of substance users versus controls. Instead, the analyses are regression/correlational (AUDIT as continuous regressor) across a continuum of drinking severity; thus it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a between-group substance-users vs controls contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (GMV via VBM), I7 (significant whole-brain foci with reported coordinates), I8 (results reported in text/tables), I9 (participant and MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (study does not perform/report a between-group users vs controls voxelwise contrast), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human MRI VBM study comparing cannabis-using participants (SCH + CAN) to non-using controls (SCH) and reports voxelwise gray-matter density results (VBM with DARTEL). The paper reports a significant cluster (left middle frontal gyrus) with MNI coordinates, cluster size and t-value from voxelwise analyses (ROI-restricted but voxelwise), and uses GM density as the outcome. Participant/sample, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM differences between substance users and controls), I5 (GM density measure), I6 (voxelwise between-group contrast reported, ROI-confined voxelwise map with coordinates), I7 (significant peak coordinates reported), I8 (results reported clearly with coordinates) and I9 (participant and MRI details provided). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only without voxelwise maps, atlas-parcellation-only, or non-empirical) are met. Although both groups are schizophrenia patients (users vs non-users), the contrast is a substance-user vs control comparison and therefore qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study that assesses grey-matter (GM) volume differences between substance users (heavy drinkers, with smoking subgroup) and controls using lobar/atlas-based volumetry. However, the analyses are ROI/parcellation-based (atlas-derived lobar GM volumes) using MANCOVA/ANCOVA and do not report any voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain statistical contrasts nor provide peak coordinates. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise results with reported significant foci (I6 and I7) and thus cannot contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports voxelwise gray-matter volume results (VBM) computed across the whole brain, with significant peak coordinates (MNI) for group contrasts (e.g., bilateral/right superior temporal gyrus, hippocampus, precentral gyrus) and corrected p-values. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis assessing GM differences between substance users and controls (alcohol class). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare college-aged binge-drinkers (alcohol users) and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (cluster-extent threshold corrected) and provides significant peak coordinates in MNI space (ventral striatum, hippocampus, amygdala, etc.). Methods include scanner field strength and preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL). Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM study), I5 (GM volume/density via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (at least one significant whole-brain cluster with coordinates), I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I9 (participant demographics, MRI details, preprocessing reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to controls and reports whole-brain GM volume differences; however the provided full text does not include the required peak coordinates for any significant whole-brain clusters. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I5 (GM volume measure via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I7 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach for significant whole-brain clusters are present in the provided text; results are referenced to Table 4/Supplement but coordinates are not available here). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Because I7 is not satisfied based on the supplied content, the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that directly compares substance users (alcohol, cocaine, and/or cannabis use disorders) to healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It reports gray matter volume (GMV) measures (volume) and performs whole-brain voxelwise analyses with topological FDR correction. The paper reports multiple significant clusters from whole-brain contrasts with peak coordinates (e.g., x = −20, y = −16, z = −26; x = 6, y = −4, z = 10; etc.), lists MRI field strength (3-T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8/DARTEL), and participant demographics. All required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) participants and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests (with and without covariates) and provides significant peak coordinates (e.g., ventral putamen x=24,y=15,z=-11; thalamus x=0,y=-13,z=10) that survive corrected thresholds. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), acquisition and preprocessing details (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL), and statistical thresholds. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4–I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Recommended for inclusion in meta-analysis of structurally altered GM in substance users (stimulants).

The study is an empirical English-language structural MRI investigation that performed whole-brain voxelwise VBM and vertexwise cortical thickness (CT) analyses and reports significant CT reductions in substance users vs. controls, so it meets I4, I5, and I6. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are reported (I9). However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the significant whole-brain CT clusters: although clusters and atlas-labels are described and figures are referenced, no explicit coordinate tables or peak coordinates are present in the supplied full text. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting at least one significant cluster with peak coordinates) is not satisfied, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although the paper is an empirical English-language VBM study comparing cocaine users and controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses with significant clusters (meeting I4, I5, I6), the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the significant whole-brain gray-matter clusters. Inclusion criterion I7 requires that at least one whole-brain contrast yields significant clusters with reported peak coordinates; this criterion is not satisfied in the supplied content. Criterion I8 (acceptable reporting in tables/figures/supplement) is also not satisfied in the provided full text, as no coordinate tables/figure captions or supplemental coordinate listings are included. Therefore the study cannot be pooled in a coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply to the content supplied.

This is an empirical English MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects to controls and uses cortical thickness and cortical volume measures with vertexwise/cluster-based whole-brain analyses. Thus I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, and participant/method details are reported (I9). However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach x,y,z) for any significant clusters nor a coordinate table in the supplied content. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates; that criterion is not met in the provided material. Supplemental data are referenced but not included here, so coordinates cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be EXCLUDED under the meta-analysis rules because I7 is not satisfied based on the provided full text.

This study compares two groups of alcohol users (recovering alcoholics vs actively drinking subjects) and does not include a healthy control group, so it does not address user vs control contrasts required for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (grey-matter measure: regional gray matter volumes reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no comparison of substance users vs non-using controls), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map with reported peak coordinates; results are region-based volumes), I7 (no significant voxelwise peaks reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only region/ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears to be limited to abstract/metadata in the provided content, so fulltext_incomplete=true. Therefore the paper is excluded.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing chronic alcohol users to controls and reports hippocampal and temporal lobe volumetry (meets I4 and I5). However, the article presents region-of-interest volumetric analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise statistical maps, and no peak coordinates or whole-brain statistical map results are provided in the available content (does not meet I6 or I7). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, only abstract/metadata content is available in the provided full text, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

The study is an empirical English-language MRI investigation using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter between amphetamine-type stimulant (ATS) users and controls (meets I4, I5). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses (meets I6) and participant/MRI details are reported (meets I9). However, the provided full-text does not include any reported peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the significant whole-brain clusters; although significant clusters are described, no peak coordinates/tables are present in the supplied content. Inclusion criterion I7 (at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates) is therefore not demonstrably met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Because the supplied full text appears to be missing coordinate tables/numeric results, I set fulltext_incomplete=true. Conclusion: EXCLUDE on the basis that I7 is not met in the provided content; recommend obtaining the complete article/tables to reassess.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract describes quantitative volumetric estimates of ventricular/CSF and regional grey-matter structures rather than reporting a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical contrast with peak coordinates. Therefore the study meets I4 (empirical English MRI comparing substance users (alcohol) to controls) and I5 (grey-matter volume measures) but does not provide evidence of I6 (a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast) or I7 (reported significant peak coordinates). This pattern corresponds to an ROI/region-volume style analysis, invoking exclusion E5. Because the full article is not provided, confirmation is limited; fulltext_incomplete flagged.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with reported peak coordinates. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical English sMRI study of AUD vs controls), I5 (uses cortical thickness, an accepted grey-matter measure), I9 (reports participant/sample and MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise AUD vs control contrast with coordinates—analyses are primarily atlas-based and targeted vertex follow-up was confined to selected regions), I7 (no reported significant whole-brain clusters with peak x,y,z coordinates from a between-group contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only ROI/parcellation-based results with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (primary between-group results derive from atlas parcellation/region-average thickness rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map). The full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical 3T MRI study measuring cortical volume, thickness and surface area (meets I4 and I5). The authors performed a vertexwise whole-brain analysis (QDEC) (meets I6) but report that the whole-brain analysis revealed no significant between-group clusters; therefore the study does not provide any significant whole-brain peaks with coordinates (fails I7). Primary reported findings are from an atlas-parcellation ROI approach (Desikan–Killiany regions) and per-region averaged analyses rather than voxelwise/vertexwise significant clusters, so it violates exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI results with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas-parcellation/regional averages). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no significant whole-brain foci reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E5, E6. Full text appears complete for screening. Consequently the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis because it provides no surviving whole-brain voxel/vertex peak coordinates to contribute.

Exclusion(s) met: E5 (study’s significant results derive from an ROI-restricted voxelwise analysis; whole-brain analyses reported in-text were null). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing substance users — long-term abstinent alcoholics — vs controls) and I5 (grey-matter measure: gray matter density/volume assessed via VBM). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 and I7 — the paper’s only surviving significant between-group findings were from an a priori ROI (amygdala/VMPFC); although voxelwise ROI results are reported (cluster sizes and corrected p-values), the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z) for these foci, and the whole-brain voxelwise contrasts yielded no significant clusters. Therefore the study cannot contribute coordinates from a qualifying whole-brain/voxelwise contrast. Full text appears complete for the main paper (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an empirical English-language MRI investigation comparing alcohol-dependent individuals and light-drinking controls and reports grey-matter volume measures (I4 and I5 satisfied). However, the MRI analyses are based on automatic segmentation into lobes and subcortical structures (lobar/regional volumetry/parcellation) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical contrast reporting peak coordinates. The paper does not provide voxelwise statistical maps or reported MNI/Talairach peak coordinates; therefore it does not meet I6 and I7. Because the between-group results derive from an atlas/parcellation approach rather than voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text considered sufficient to assess these criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM8 with random-field cluster-size correction and reports multiple significant clusters (with reported MNI/Talairach cursor coordinates and cluster details) for group and sex-specific contrasts. MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing (New Segment, DARTEL), statistical software, and participant age/sex/substance-use characteristics are described. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4–I9 (whole-brain voxelwise GM volume results with reported significant foci). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an empirical English-language VBM MRI comparison including a schizophrenia with SUD group (substance users) versus healthy controls, reporting voxelwise gray-matter density results with Talairach coordinates in the ventral striatum. It uses a voxelwise VBM approach (GM density), reports MRI field strength and preprocessing (SPM2), and provides significant peak coordinates from the voxelwise ROI analysis (small-volume correction within the striatum). Although the analysis used an a priori striatal ROI/SVC, the results are voxelwise with reported coordinates, which meets the meta-analysis criterion allowing voxelwise maps confined to a sub-volume. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

Full text content appears limited to abstract/metadata and describes region-based volumetric analyses (regional brain measures, structure volumes and correlations) rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with reported peak coordinates. Therefore the study does not meet whole-brain voxelwise evidence requirements (I6) nor the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain cluster with coordinates (I7). It meets inclusion criteria I4 and I5 (empirical MRI study assessing grey-matter volume differences). It is excluded because it reports only ROI/regional volumetry with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (Exclusion E5). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), which reduces certainty of this determination.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing 27 heroin-dependent (MMT) patients to 23 healthy controls (I4). The primary grey-matter measure is GM volume (VBM modulated GM segments) (I5). The authors performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM5/ VBM5 and explicit voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and describe whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6). The manuscript reports multiple significant clusters and discusses their locations and Brodmann areas, describes conversion of MNI to Talairach coordinates via GingerALE, and states that locations/extent are presented in tables/figures, satisfying the allowance for coordinate reporting in tables/figures (I7, I8). Participant demographics, substance use details, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using hippocampal subfield volumes derived from FreeSurfer (satisfies I4 and I5). However, the paper does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise or vertexwise between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates; analyses are based on ROI/subfield volumetric comparisons (no voxelwise maps or reported x,y,z peaks). Therefore it fails I6 and I7. This violates the meta-analysis requirements and meets exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derive from region-based segmentation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study should be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of gray matter comparing substance users (crack-cocaine ± alcohol) to controls and reports regional cortical volume reductions (prefrontal). However, the study used predefined regional ROI quantification (Talairach/Brodmann ROIs) and reported per-region volume differences rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map with peak coordinates. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise results or peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that directly compares grey-matter volume between cocaine users (a stimulant class) and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5/VBM5.1) with significant between-group clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., left VLPFC BA44 at x=-37,y=18,z=29; left OFC BA11 at x=-20,y=28,z=-20), and provides participant, MRI field-strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistics details. Thus it fulfills whole-brain, coordinate-based inclusion criteria and is relevant to stimulants. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for extraction.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls reporting GM volume differences, but the structural analysis is ROI-based (WFU PickAtlas/MarsBaR) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise analysis. The paper does not report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts with significant peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analysis). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM volume measures), I9 (participant/sample details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast reported), I7 (no significant cluster peak coordinates from a whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete.

This study does not compare substance users to non-user controls, which is required by the review objective. It reports voxel-based morphometry (GM volume) differences between subgroups of smokers (quitters vs relapsers) rather than a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus healthy controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I4 (must compare substance users to controls), I6 (must report a whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls), and I7 (that whole-brain contrast must yield at least one significant cluster with coordinates). The study does meet I5 (uses grey-matter VBM measures) and I9 (reports participant/substance/MRI details). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) from the list are directly met. Full text appears complete. Consequently, exclude from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study assessing grey-matter (cortical thickness) differences using whole-brain vertexwise analyses (FreeSurfer QDEC) and reports significant clusters (frontal, superior frontal, superior parietal, etc.). Thus I4, I5, I6, and I9 are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not report peak voxel/vertex coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the significant clusters in the main text, tables, or the supplied supplementary excerpt. Inclusion criterion I7 explicitly requires at least one significant whole-brain contrast with reported peak coordinates. Because those coordinates are not present in the provided article content (and cannot be verified in supplementary files here), the study does not meet I7 and therefore cannot contribute coordinates to a coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Exclusion reason: fails I7 (no reported peak coordinates).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing chronic cannabis users and controls (meets I4). It reports grey-matter volume and concentration measures (modulated and unmodulated VBM; meets I5). Voxelwise statistical maps/contrasts are reported with peak coordinates (MNI) for significant hippocampal clusters; analyses include a hippocampal sub-volume voxelwise map with reported coordinates, which qualifies under the allowance for sub-volume voxelwise maps (meets I6 and I7). Results and coordinates are presented in text/tables/figures (meets I8). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported (meets I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply.

Excluded because the study’s between-group analyses were performed on parcel-averaged cortical thickness measures derived from the FreeSurfer Desikan–Killiany 34-region parcellation and tested in SPSS, not as voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with reported stereotactic peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls) and I5 (uses a grey-matter surface-based measure: cortical thickness). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast reported) and I7 (no significant whole-brain clusters with reported x,y,z coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derived from a predefined atlas parcellation rather than a voxel/vertexwise map). E5 also applies because only region-based (parcellation/ROI-style) between-group results are reported with no qualifying whole-brain voxel/vertexwise findings. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study cannot contribute coordinates for the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

Exclusion summary: This empirical structural MRI study of heavy smokers vs controls meets inclusion criteria I4 (empirical English MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I5 (uses grey-matter measure: cortical thickness), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). However, it does NOT meet I6 and I7: the reported analyses are region-wise (Destrieux atlas) per-region cortical thickness comparisons entered into SPSS/ANCOVA and FDR-corrected; no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map or between-group contrast is reported, and no significant peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are provided. Thus exclusion criteria E6 (results derived from a predefined atlas parcellation with per-region averages) and E5 (only ROI/region-wise analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast with reported coordinates (I6 and I7 not met; E5 and E6 met).

This study is excluded because it reports only region-based/parcellation analyses (FreeSurfer-derived regional volumes and summed bilateral ROIs) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map with reported peak coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation/region averages rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I5 (GM measures: volumes/thickness), I9 (reports participant and MRI details). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with coordinates) and I7 (no reported significant peak coordinates from a whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete for evaluation.

This is a within-subject correlational study of alcohol users (n=23) without a healthy control group and therefore does not perform any whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts of substance users vs. controls. The paper reports ROI-based measures (insular gray matter volume and gyrification) extracted using atlas parcellations (Neuromorphometrics, Desikan-Killiany) and regression analyses within the user sample rather than whole-brain group comparisons with reported peak coordinates. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (only ROI analyses/no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas-based per-region measures rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (grey-matter measures: volume/gyrification) and I9 (reported participant age/sex and MRI parameters). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (no substance-user vs control group comparison), I6 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrast), I7 (no significant between-group foci with reported coordinates). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study assessing grey-matter using surface-based cortical thickness measures (meeting I4 and I5). The authors conducted a whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analysis with hemispheric average and age covariates and permutation-based multiple-comparison correction (meeting I6). The study reports a surviving significant cluster in left superior frontal cortex with Talairach peak coordinates x = -15.3, y = 61.8, z = 5.0 and cluster p = 0.024 (meeting I7 and I8). Participant demographic details, MRI field strength (1.5T), scan parameters, and statistical software/procedures are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and the paper is empirical original research. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structural GM differences between substance users and controls.

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of methamphetamine-dependent individuals vs. healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (satisfying I4 and I5) and it reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition details (satisfying I9), the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates. Instead, the VBM-processed data were summarized as average modulated gray-matter volumes extracted from 70 atlas-defined ROIs and reported as ROI-based results (including a thalamic LD ROI). No voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with MNI/Talairach coordinates or surviving cluster peaks is provided. Therefore it violates the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain, coordinate-based results and must be excluded per E5 (only ROI analyses/no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise/vertexwise maps). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7.

Exclusion justified because the study reports only per-region volumetric comparisons derived from segmentation/parcellation (CMA and FreeSurfer) rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with reported peak coordinates. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain results), E6 (results derived from atlas/parcellation per-region volumes). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing grey-matter volumes between alcohol users and controls), I5 (grey-matter measures: regional volumes of cortex and subcortical GM). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast reported), I7 (no significant whole-brain clusters with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not provide the required voxelwise coordinates for coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

Although this is an empirical MRI study that performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses of grey-matter density (and reports participant demographics and MRI details), the VBM results yielded no significant between-group differences. Inclusion criterion I7 requires that at least one whole-brain between-group contrast yields at least one significant cluster with reported peak coordinates. Because no significant GM clusters were reported, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study is empirical, in English, and uses VBM-derived GM density measures in alcohol users vs controls (meets I4 and I5). It also reports demographic and MRI details (meets I9). However, the paper does not present a conventional whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group statistical contrast of GM (AUD vs HC) with reported peak coordinates (x,y,z). The authors performed joint-ICA and tested group differences on component loading coefficients, and although spatial component maps are described, the provided full text does not report voxelwise between-group contrasts or peak coordinates, nor point to coordinate tables in the available content (fails I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria from E5–E7 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM contrast with reported significant peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of smokers vs controls (I4) using cortical thickness as a grey-matter measure (I5) and reports participant/sample/MRI details including field strength and FreeSurfer processing (I9). However, the paper does not present a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map with reported peak coordinates: primary analyses use a composite frontal cortical-thickness measure and per-region (FreeSurfer parcel) tests, and no whole-brain significant foci with x,y,z coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. The results are thus derived from region-of-interest / atlas-parcellation analyses, invoking exclusion criteria E5 and E6. Consequently the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between non-treatment-seeking cocaine-dependent individuals and non-drug-using controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., left middle frontal gyrus x=−33 y=23 z=37) and provides methodological details (3T scanner, SPM8/VBM8 preprocessing, participant ages, substance-use characteristics). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing male polysubstance users to controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant GM volume differences. It therefore satisfies I4 (empirical MRI study), I5 (GM volume measure via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise contrast), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the significant whole-brain clusters; no tables/figures/supplementary with coordinates are present in the supplied content. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one significant cluster with reported peak coordinates; this is not met in the provided material. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis unless full-text tables/figures with peak coordinates are provided.

Exclusion: This study reports regional/subcortical volumes derived from automated FreeSurfer parcellation and hippocampal subfield segmentation (atlas-based ROI measures) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map with peak coordinates. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E5 (ROI-only analyses/no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than voxelwise maps). Inclusion met: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I5 (grey-matter measures including regional volumes/cortical thickness), and I9 (reports age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map reported), I7 (no significant whole-brain peaks with coordinates reported), and I8 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures provided). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The paper is an empirical MRI study of cannabis users vs controls using cortical thickness (satisfies I4 and I5). However, I cannot verify that it reports a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with at least one significant cluster and reported peak coordinates (I6 and I7). The text references a vertex-based analysis in the Supplement (eTable 2) but the supplementary materials/coordinate tables are not provided here. Because those whole-brain coordinate data cannot be confirmed in the available full text, the study cannot be confirmed to meet I6 and I7 and therefore cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are demonstrably met based on the available text. Full text appears lacking the supplementary coordinate tables necessary to confirm voxel/vertex-level significant foci.

This is an empirical, whole-brain vertexwise cortical thickness MRI study comparing ayahuasca (psychedelic) users to controls and reports significant clusters with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I5 (uses cortical thickness as GM measure), I6 (vertexwise whole-brain analysis using FreeSurfer), I7 (reports significant clusters with coordinates), I8 (results reported in tables/figures), I9 (participant and MRI details reported). However, the study does NOT address the review objective drug classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants): it examines psychedelic/ayahuasca users (DMT). Therefore it does not meet the review’s topical requirement and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria E5–E7 are triggered by the methods. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of prescription opioid users vs controls that reports gray-matter measures via voxel-based morphometry (GMV) and provides participant and acquisition details. However, the paper’s morphometry results are reported as ROI-based GMV comparisons (extraction from a priori L.NAc seed and the rsFC-derived L.vmPFC cluster) rather than as a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with reported peak coordinates. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results or significant peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This longitudinal empirical MRI study reports whole-brain vertexwise/vertexwise surface-based analyses of cortical thickness (a grey-matter measure acceptable per I5) comparing alcohol initiators versus non-users. The paper provides whole-brain between-group contrasts computed with FreeSurfer, reports significant clusters (right middle frontal gyrus) with peak Talairach coordinates (per Table 3), and describes methods and subject demographics (age, sex, scanner). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results (including cluster tables/figures), and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical English structural MRI study comparing smokers (n=22) and never-smokers (n=21). It reports surface-based cortical thickness (a permitted GM measure) and performs a whole-brain vertexwise analysis (FreeSurfer) with multiple-comparison correction, yielding a significant cluster in left medial OFC with reported Talairach coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing cannabis users vs. non-users (meets I4). The study reports grey-matter volume analyses (GM volume) and uses whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 VBM analyses (meets I5 and I6). The whole-brain contrast yielded significant clusters (e.g., reduced right anterior cingulum reaching FWE significance p=0.001) and the manuscript indicates region-wise results from the voxelwise maps (meets I7 and I8). The paper reports participant demographics, substance use characterization, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, SPSS) meeting I9. Methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas/parcellation-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the coordinate-based meta-analysis of grey-matter differences in substance users vs controls.

While this is an empirical, English-language MRI study of cannabis-using vs non-using MS patients that analyzes grey matter volume (I4, I5 satisfied), it does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of substance users versus controls with at least one significant cluster and peak coordinates. The main voxelwise analysis is a behavioural PLS (brain–behaviour correlations) and region-of-interest correlations; the paper explicitly reports no group differences in total GM/WM volume and does not present a significant whole-brain cannabis>control or control>cannabis voxelwise GM contrast with peak coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. None of the specified exclusion criteria (E5–E7) strictly apply, so exclusion is due to failure to meet required inclusion items (I6, I7). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing smokers (substance users: nicotine) vs nonsmoker controls, using whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray matter volume. The paper reports at least one significant whole-brain GMV cluster with peak coordinates (left medial OFC, X=−4.5, Y=66, Z=−16.5) and cluster size/statistics, satisfying the requirement for reported significant foci. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12/SPM12) are reported. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria for structural whole-brain GM comparisons are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not atlas-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume and density between smokers and never-smokers. The Methods describe whole-brain VBM preprocessing and SPM2 analyses, and the Results report significant between-group clusters (FDR-corrected P<0.05) with localization via Talairach coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for reported peak coordinates from a voxelwise whole-brain contrast. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for voxelwise whole-brain grey-matter differences and reports significant foci suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Excluded because the paper does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map with reported peak coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports primarily lobar/ROI and global measures with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise results) and E6 (between-group results are derived from atlas/parcellation-based regional averages using FreeSurfer labels). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences in alcohol users vs controls), I5 (reports grey-matter measures including cortical thickness and cortical volume), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with coordinates are provided) and I7 (no significant cluster peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports ROI-based analyses and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group SPM-style contrast with reported peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports grey-matter measures—regional GM volumes), I9 (reports participant demographics and MRI details). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (study population is first-episode schizophrenia patients vs healthy controls, not a substance-user group vs controls), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise statistical map reported), I7 (no significant whole-brain clusters with peak coordinates reported). Full-text completeness: full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the key requirement of whole-brain voxelwise substance-user vs control contrasts and must be excluded from the substance-use GM meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare chronic cigarette smokers (n=44) with matched non-smoker controls, reporting significant clusters of reduced gray matter in smokers. It measures modulated gray matter volume (VBM), performed voxel-wise two-sample t-tests in SPM5 across the whole brain with cluster-level reporting (see Fig.1 and Table 1). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical methods are reported. The manuscript contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not violate exclusion criteria E5–E7.

This study is an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing older smokers and never-smokers and reports gray-matter density differences and detailed participant/method data (satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I9). However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the significant whole-brain clusters; inclusion criterion I7 explicitly requires reported peak coordinates for at least one significant whole-brain contrast. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I7 (significant foci with reported peak coordinates) based on the provided full text.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare young adult male smokers (nicotine users) and matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8/DARTEL) of gray matter volume with multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and describes multiple significant clusters and regional results (figures/tables referenced). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The paper therefore satisfies: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I5 (GM volume measure), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I7 (significant whole-brain clusters reported), I8 (results available in tables/figures), and I9 (demographics and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

Although this is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing smoking (nicotine) groups with non-smokers and reporting whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I4, I5, I6, and I9), the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for the significant clusters (no x,y,z coordinates in MNI or Talairach space are given in the text/tables provided). Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates; that criterion is not satisfied based on the supplied full text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (not flagged as incomplete), but coordinate reporting is absent, so the study cannot contribute coordinate data to the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical English MRI study of nicotine (cigarette) users with GM volumetric measures using FreeSurfer (meets I4, I5) and reports participant/MRI details (I9). However, all reported between-group comparisons are regional/parcellation-based (FreeSurfer lobar and subcortical volumes) rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps; no voxel coordinates or peak foci are reported. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Consequently, it meets exclusion criteria E5 (ROI/parcellation-only with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from an atlas/parcellation). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of methamphetamine (a stimulant) users vs controls that reports grey-matter measures (VBM GMD and ROI subcortical volumes) and performs whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL-VBM). However, although voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts are described and significant clusters are reported in the text, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any significant whole-brain cluster. Inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one whole-brain contrast to yield a significant cluster with reported peak coordinates. Because those coordinates are not present in the supplied full text (and cannot be verified in figures/tables/supplementary materials here), the study does not meet I7 and therefore cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English MRI study of smoking and brain volumes (satisfies I4 and I5), but it does not report voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates. The paper presents global and regional volumetric measures and regression b-values (total brain, cerebrum, gray matter, etc.) rather than voxelwise/coordinate-based clusters. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (only region-based/volumetric results; no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=21) to healthy controls (n=21) reporting grey-matter/subcortical volume differences. The paper uses vertexwise analysis (FSL Randomize) to produce vertexwise statistical maps showing significant surface deformations (reductions) in multiple subcortical GM regions (thalamus, putamen, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens, etc.). The manuscript reports MNI coordinates in figure annotations and describes vertex/voxelwise results and cluster-level significance (FDR-corrected p≤0.05). Participant age/sex, substance-use measures (AUDIT-K, SMAST, lifetime drinking history), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (FSL, SIENAX, FIRST, Randomize) are provided. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I4–I9 (empirical GM MRI comparison, appropriate GM measures, vertexwise whole-brain/subvolume maps with significant foci and reported coordinates, and reporting of key sample/MRI details). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used FreeSurfer-derived regional (ROI) volumetric analyses comparing smokers and non-smokers (per-region percentages of ICV) and generalized linear models on these ROI volumes. No voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map or between-group contrast with reported peak coordinates is provided. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain voxelwise results for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I5 (grey-matter volume measures reported), I9 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast reported), I7 (no significant peak coordinates reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (results derived from atlas/parcellation regional volumes rather than voxelwise maps). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Consequently, exclude from coordinate-based GM meta-analysis.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (GM volume) analyses within samples of smokers (relapsed vs abstinent) but does not include any between-group whole-brain contrast comparing substance users (smokers) to healthy controls. Therefore it does not satisfy the primary inclusion requirement for the review (I4: comparison of substance users vs controls) nor the requirement that the paper report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls (I6) or a significant foci from such a contrast (I7). The study does meet I5 (uses GM volume measures) and I9 (reports participant age/sex and MRI details). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical MRI investigation comparing smokers and controls and reports voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density) results (I4, I5, I9). However, although VBM was performed and group differences (reduced GM density in dlPFC and insula/operculum) are reported, the provided full text does not present voxelwise peak coordinates or explicit whole-brain statistical maps required by the meta-analysis (fails I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Therefore it cannot contribute coordinates to the coordinate-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing older smokers (successful and unsuccessful quitters) with never-smokers and reporting voxelwise whole-brain analyses of grey-matter density using tensor-based morphometry in SPM5. The paper reports significant between-group clusters (UQ vs NS, SQ vs NS), describes the voxelwise methodology, statistical thresholds, and references Supplementary Table S2 (where peak coordinates and detailed cluster information are provided). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM comparisons, GM measure (density), whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, availability of significant foci (reported in supplement), and acceptable reporting of methodological details. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.
